errors.english: "Does the cause produce the effect by meeting it, or without meeting it?" Since I have said this, the same challenge
errors.why: The opponents quote the Madhyamika's own question back at him: 'As for what you said, does the cause produce the effect by meeting it or not, the same challenge applies to you'; it is not their question, and 'Since I have said this' gets the speaker wrong.

fix.find: "Does the cause produce the effect by meeting it, or without meeting it?" Since I have said this, the same challenge
fix.replace: "As for what you said, 'Does the cause produce the effect by meeting it, or without meeting it?', the same challenge

errors.english: therefore, the effect is not something to be known
errors.why: ཤེས་བྱ here stands for ཞེས་བྱ in the root verse: 'then there is no so-called effect', not 'the effect is not knowable'.

note: The Prāsaṅgika argument comes through, but the opening of the opponent's tu quoque makes the Madhyamika the speaker of what the opponent is quoting.

errors.english: Because there is no ignorance separate from the different actions.
errors.why: ལས is the ablative after བདག (end of the previous side): 'because there is no ignorance different from the self'. It is not 'actions'.

fix.find: Because there is no ignorance separate from the different actions.
fix.replace: Because there is no ignorance different from [the self].

errors.english: the view of a self (satkayadrishti) the view of a personal identity
errors.why: སེམས་ཅན་ལྟ་བ is the view of a sentient being (sattvadṛṣṭi), not satkāyadṛṣṭi ('jig tshogs la lta ba); the verse is also turned into prose.

note: The argument against the Vedāntin self is followed in outline, but the opening misreads the ablative and some technical terms are approximate.

errors.english: the Blessed One spoke the following to demonstrate the faults of abiding:
errors.why: བཅོམ་ལྡན་འདས་ is a vocative. Subhūti addresses the Blessed One ('Blessed One, furthermore...'), as the humble verb forms (མངོན་པར་འདུ་བགྱི་བ, མ་ལགས) show; the Buddha is not the speaker.

fix.find: the Blessed One spoke the following to demonstrate the faults of abiding:
fix.replace: to demonstrate the faults of abiding, [the sūtra] says, addressing the Blessed One: Blessed One,

errors.english: the Blessed One said: In this way, form is not something to be grasped
errors.why: Here too བཅོམ་ལྡན་འདས་ is a vocative addressed to the Buddha (the verb is the humble མ་མཆིས), so it is not a statement by the Buddha.

fix.find: the Blessed One said: In this way
fix.replace: [the sūtra] says: Blessed One, in this way

errors.why: The Tibetan says 'this form is the self' (identification of form with self), not 'mine'.

note: The commentary itself is rendered accurately, but the sūtra passages Subhūti addresses to the Buddha are twice given as spoken by the Buddha.

errors.english: there is no non-engagement; this is the fifth unshared quality.
errors.why: This completes the fifth āveṇika quality: the notion of difference (ཐ་དད་པའི་འདུ་ཤེས, previous side) 'does not occur'. 'No non-engagement' says the opposite.

note: Apart from the garbled opening fragment, this is a faithful rendering of the commentary on the unshared qualities.

errors.english: This text explains the characteristics of flawed scripture and the principles of logical reasoning.
errors.why: The side opens with the last item of a list ('...and the characteristic of teaching a completely impure scripture'). The summary sentence is the translator's own, and the next sentence repeats a definition that is given later in the side.

fix.find: This text explains the characteristics of flawed scripture and the principles of logical reasoning.

errors.english: regarding the characteristic of universal observation and its examples
errors.why: The Tibetan is 'the characteristic of observing similarity with something else' (anyatva-sārūpya), not 'universal similarity' (ཐམས་ཅད་མཐུན་པ), which is the subject of the following clause.

errors.english: By abandoning the afflictions of both the mundane and supramundane worlds
errors.why: 'Mundane and supramundane' describes the abandonment and its fruit, not the afflictions.

note: Mostly follows the Saṃdhinirmocana list of reasoning characteristics, but adds an invented framing sentence and blurs the terms that tell the cases apart.

errors.english: the nature of concealed truth and relative truth
errors.why: The Tibetan names relative and ultimate truth (saṃvṛti and paramārtha).

fix.find: the nature of concealed truth and relative truth
fix.replace: the nature of relative and ultimate truth

errors.english: the stage of arising and the stage of the arisen
errors.why: བསྐྱེད་པ་དང་རྫོགས་པའི་རིམ་པ are the generation stage and the completion stage.

fix.find: the stage of arising and the stage of the arisen
fix.replace: the generation stage and the completion stage

errors.english:
Having the nature of qualities and enjoyment
Is Vajradhara's characteristic.
errors.why: This is prose commentary: 'by this, Vajradhara as having the form of the dharmakāya and sambhogakāya'. It is set as verse, and dharma- and sambhoga[kāya] are read as 'qualities and enjoyment'.

errors.english: the nature of the dharmakāya, sambhogakāya, and nirmāṇakāya
errors.why: Only the dharmakāya and sambhogakāya are named; the nirmāṇakāya is added.

errors.english: This interpretation, which has been passed down through a lineage of transmission, is favored by some.
errors.why: The Tibetan says 'this is the explanation according to the genuine tradition'; 'favored by some' is not in it.

note: Readable and close in its verses, but the doctrinal summary garbles the two truths and the two stages, and part of the prose is recast as verse.

errors.english: Taking what is not given has been discourse continues to next page
errors.why: The words 'discourse continues to next page' are an editorial note left in the translation; the Tibetan simply continues 'has been [condemned] by the Blessed One'.

fix.find: Taking what is not given has been discourse continues to next page
fix.replace: Taking what is not given has been [condemned] by the Blessed One…

note: A faithful rendering of the pārājika instruction from the ordination ritual, marred only by a stray editorial note at the end.
A faithful rendering of this difficult commentary on the six types of arhat and the conditions for falling away.

errors.why: རྗེས་སུ་འཇུག here is grammatical carry-over (anuvṛtti): the word 'of the effect' is supplied from the previous sūtra. It is not a phrase meaning 'follows as an effect'.

errors.english: even cognition characterized by being produced from that cause
errors.why: རྟགས་ཅན་ཤེས་པ is the cognition of the inferred (liṅgin), i.e. the inferential cognition arising from it; it is not 'cognition characterized by'.

note: The treatment of pseudo-reasons is sound, but the commentary's grammatical glosses are sometimes taken as content.
A faithful rendering of the rain verses and Śakra's speech from the fish jātaka, with the verse and the moral both intact.
